structured.approach: I used the data-engineering-steps skill for the DE-01 procedure. I read both contracted inputs (feat.tasks, org.engineering_stack). The step's hook blocks all shell commands, so I checked the ap_pipeline checkout with file tools instead: Glob for the layout, Grep for Databricks/Spark/JDBC references (none), and Read on the .git files (HEAD, the refs for main, dev and feature/story, the feature/story reflog, config), ci.py, __init__.py and schedule.json. I compared these with the tool view. I needed no connector (osv, pypi) because the inputs and checkout held every fact. I wrote task.repo_access with nine prerequisite checks and four non-blocking observations.
tools_used: Bash (attempted; denied by G9 hook for DE-01)

claims.text: No repository uses Databricks or a database, so Databricks access is not applicable to ap_pipeline.
Repository ap_pipeline (Python 3.9, standard library) is available locally and the agent identity has write access; git status is clean.
Branch feature/story was created from dev at 3fcbe1b and is checked out; main and dev both point at 3fcbe1b.
The Data Engineering tasks in scope are TSK-01 (STORY-01) and TSK-02 (STORY-02), both on the ap_pipeline repository, so no new repository is needed.
The CI command is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and enforces line coverage >= 90% plus static checks.
ap_pipeline is at version 0.4.0 today and TSK-01 owns the version step.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package, while the repository memory says standard library.
Only main and dev have an upstream configured in .git/config; remote origin is github.com/arghya05/ap-pipeline-sample.
schedule.json sets a daily run at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata and is on TSK-01's must-not-change list.

open_questions: RA-1 (non-blocking): The feature branch is named feature/story rather than feature/<story> (e.g. feature/STORY-01). Should both Data Engineering stories share it? Interim: yes, with story-ID commit prefixes.
RA-2 (non-blocking): This step could not confirm that the coverage package that ci.py needs is installed for /usr/bin/python3, because shell commands are not allowed here.
RA-3 (non-blocking): feature/story has no upstream configured and this step did not test a push. Write access rests on the tool view, and the spine pushes at DE-10.
structured.summary: DE-01 is ready. ap_pipeline is available locally with write access for the agent identity, and the feature branch feature/story is checked out from dev at 3fcbe1b. No new repository is needed for TSK-01 and TSK-02. Databricks is not applicable because no repository uses Databricks or a database. I recorded three non-blocking open questions (branch naming, the coverage dependency in ci.py, push not tested) and one note that schedule.json is out of scope until DE-13. There are no blocking questions. Output: task.repo_access.md.

tool_input.command: git branch -a && git status --short --branch && git log --oneline -3 && git remote -v && ls -R src tests | head -40 && grep -n version src/ap_pipeline/__init__.py; test -w . && echo writable; grep -ril databricks . --include=* 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^./.git/' | head
tool_input.description: Inspect repo branches, status, layout and write access
